(This evening through Friday)...
Issued at 219 PM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

Surface analysis this afternoon shows high pressure east of Indiana, 
over the middle Atlantic states. A warm front was found over IA, 
extending east into NRN IL. The remnants of a thunderstorm cluster 
was riding the front over nrn IL. Light SE flow was in place across 
Central Indiana. High convective debris clouds were found over 
northern Indiana, moving east and dissipating. The cloud system from 
the tropical system approaching the gulf coast was spreading 
northward across KY and TN. Dew points across Indiana were in the 
upper 40s to lower 50s.

Tonight...

Partly cloudy skies will be expected this evening as the clouds 
across the northern half of the state continue to progress eastward 
while the cloud shield from the south makes steady progression north. 
The cloud shield should arrive overnight, providing high clouds. 
Forecast soundings show this saturation aloft arriving overnight, 
with very dry conditions within the lower levels. Thus increasing 
clouds will be expected tonight. With the increasing clouds across 
the area, overnight lows will be slightly warmer, in the lower 50s.

Saturday...

Little overall change is expected on Saturday. The tropical system 
to the south will continue to progress northward, spreading mid and 
high cloud cover across Central Indiana through the day The lower 
levels look to remain dry. HRRR suggests some initial bands of rain 
could arrive across southern Indiana by late afternoon and early 
evening, but overall most the day should be mostly cloudy. 
Temperatures will be somewhat warm and more humid with the arrival 
of a tropical air mass. Look for highs around 80.

Saturday Night and Sunday...

This window of time will be the most impactful from the Hurricane 
remnants. Models show the mid level low pushing to KY and across 
eastern KY on Saturday Night and Sunday respectively. Cyclonic flow 
will provide ample forcing for moisture that will spread across the 
northwest side of the system and rain pops will be high. Forecast 
soundings suggest pwats around 1.5 inches. Best wrap around moisture 
will be across SE central Indiana, including places like Rushville, 
North Vernon, Greensburg and Columbus. Thus, highest pops will be 
used in those locations. Farther north, at LAF and OKK, moisture may 
not even reach these places, and much lower pops will be used.  

Sunday Night...

Forecast soundings show dry air and top down subsidence building in 
the column on Sunday Night. This will be due to the departure of the 
remnants to the middle Atlantic states and the arrival of strong 
upper ridging over the Mississippi valley, building eastward. This 
will allow a surface high along with its associated ridge axis to 
build across Indiana from the south. Overall, decreasing cloudiness 
on Sunday Night. 

Monday...

Some upper ridging will bring quiet and warm weather to the area on 
Monday. Highs will reach the lower and middle 80s.

Tuesday...

A cold front will move through on Tuesday. The front won't have much 
moisture to work with, so will only have some low PoPs for parts of 
the area. Highs will generally be in the lower 80s.

Wednesday and beyond...

An upper trough across the southwestern USA will eject and phase 
with a northern stream trough, creating a large upper system that 
will influence the eastern half of the country into the first part 
of the weekend. This will bring first a warm front then a potent 
cold front through the area.

As is typical with these situations, there remains a good amount of 
uncertainty in the details. Will thus have broad, mainly chance 
category PoPs for Wednesday through Friday.

Highs will be in the 70s Wednesday and Thursday, and some 80s are 
possible depending on how the system develops. Cooler air will begin 
arriving on Friday, with highs in the 60s.

Some guidance has next Saturday's afternoon temperatures only in the 
40s, with a potential frost that night. Will keep an eye on it.
